chain.label: FAA oversight of operator's risk management inadequate; no SMS requirement for Part 135
chain.trigger: Contributing to the accident was the Federal Aviation Administration's inadequate oversight of the operator's risk management program and failure to require Title 14 CFR Part 135 operators to establish safety management system programs

chain.label: Survival Flight's inadequate management of safety and poor safety culture (pressure to fly, punitive repercussions, no SMS)
chain.trigger: Survival Flight's inadequate management of safety, which normalized pilots' and operations control specialists' noncompliance with risk analysis procedures

chain.label: No preflight risk analysis or shift-change briefing completed for the accident flight
chain.trigger: neither pilot completed a preflight risk assessment for the flight, as required by Title 14 Code of Federal Regulations Part 135.617

caused_by.evidence: Survival Flight's poor safety culture likely influenced the accident pilot's decision to conduct the accident flight without a shift change briefing, including an adequate preflight risk assessment
the POI's oversight of the Survival Flight flight risk assessment (FRA) was inadequate because it failed to identify that the FRA did not meet the requirements of 14 CFR 135.617

chain.label: OCC/operations control specialist accepted flight without obtaining prior-refusal or en route weather information
chain.trigger: a review of recorded phone conversations revealed the ERT did not report that the flight had been previously refused, and the OCS did not ask

caused_by.evidence: the OCS ... advised the pilot 'that it is a go, and that, you know, we need to go, regardless ... we need to launch for the flight'

chain.label: HEMS Weather Tool radar overlay omits TDWR data, hiding snow bands along the route
chain.trigger: The current version of the HEMS Weather Tool does not incorporate terminal doppler weather radar data to display precipitation

chain.label: Snow, icing AIRMET, and reduced visibility along the route not identified by pilots or OCS
chain.trigger: their failure to obtain complete en route information precluded them from identifying crucial meteorological risks for the accident flight

caused_by.evidence: resulted in the initiation of the flight without a comprehensive preflight weather evaluation
Neither the evening shift pilot nor the accident pilot were made aware that two other operators had turned down the flight request
the snow showers identified on the TDWR were not detected or displayed on the HEMS Weather Tool above the accident site

chain.label: Night VFR flight accepted and launched into forecast snow showers and areas of IMC
chain.trigger: About 28 seconds later, the evening shift pilot accepted the flight ... the accident pilot arrived at Base 14, she proceeded directly to the already-started helicopter and departed

caused_by.evidence: the evening shift pilot reviewed the weather in 28 seconds, which was likely not sufficient time to conduct a thorough review of each available weather product
the pilots likely felt pressured to meet the 7-minute timeframe for takeoff

chain.label: Night conditions before civil twilight, waning crescent moon, no night vision goggles carried
chain.trigger: sunrise occurred at 0739 and the beginning of civil twilight occurred at 0711 ... The evening shift pilot asked the accident pilot if she needed the night vision goggles and she told him that she did not

chain.label: Inadvertent IMC encounter in the second, higher-intensity snow band
chain.trigger: the pilot likely encountered IMC inadvertently when the helicopter flew through a snow band, which resulted in decreased visibility

caused_by.evidence: leading to the pilot's inadvertent encounter with instrument meteorological conditions
Night visual meteorological conditions existed at the departure location, but available weather information indicated that snow showers and areas of IMC existed along the route of flight

chain.label: IIMC escape turn flown without commanding a climb; collective reduced during 180-degree left turn
chain.trigger: the pilot began a 180° turn as part of an IIMC escape maneuver, in keeping with standard operating procedures but did not maintain altitude

caused_by.evidence: In an attempt to recover from the inadvertent instrument meteorological conditions (IIMC) encounter, the pilot began a 180° turn

chain.label: Uncommanded/unarrested descent from about 2,400 ft to below 1,300 ft toward the terrain
chain.trigger: she did not command the helicopter to climb, and it continued to descend until the last moments of the flight

caused_by.evidence: allowed the helicopter to descend until it was too late to arrest the descent and execute a climb above the trees

chain.label: Forested hills rising to 700-1,100 ft elevation beneath the flightpath
chain.trigger: The helicopter wreckage was located on a tree-covered hill ... The terrain in this area varied between 700 ft and 1,100 ft of elevation

chain.label: Descent into treetop proximity; late power application producing two overtorque events
chain.trigger: two overtorque events occurred about 8 and 3 seconds, respectively, before the end of recorded data ... consistent with the pilot responding to either an HTAWS alert or perceived imminent ground contact

caused_by.evidence: the helicopter continued to descend until the last moments of the flight
collided with forested terrain about 4 miles northeast of Zaleski, Ohio

chain.label: Collision with trees and terrain; helicopter destroyed
chain.trigger: the helicopter initially collided with a tree at a height about 30 ft above the ground on a heading of about 345°

caused_by.evidence: did not maintain altitude and allowed the helicopter to descend until it impacted terrain

chain.label: Pilot, flight nurse, and flight paramedic fatally injured
chain.trigger: The certificated commercial pilot, flight nurse, and flight paramedic died, and the helicopter was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: Her cause of death was multiple blunt force injuries
